conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice. Velocity densities are equivalence classes modulo Lebesgue-almost-everywhere equality in X, with norm ∫(1+|v|²/v₀²)|f(v)|dv and v₀>0. Gain integrals use Borel representatives and define output classes.
The angular measure is normalized area measure on S², with total mass one. Reflection is v′=v−((v−w)·n)n and w′=w+((v−w)·n)n; the parameter measure is dv dw dσ(n).

Π=m∫(v−u)⊗(v−u)F dv is a positive-semidefinite momentum-flux covariance. It enters momentum flux with a plus sign; the corresponding tensile stress would be −Π. Tensor divergence contracts the second index.

The physical model uses a normalized homogeneous one-particle velocity density and a prescribed positive rate λ independent of relative speed. Factorized incoming pairs are adopted assumptions, without a microscopic derivation or empirical calibration.
The Gaussian-mixture class has one common mean u and covariance matrices satisfying aI≤Σ≤bI with 0<a<b; closure is taken in X.

The entropy theorem uses the specific initial density ½γ(aI,u)+½γ(bI,u), with 0<a<b. H=∫f log(v₀³f)dv is dimensionless; S_B=−k_B H has entropy units and is a one-particle reference information functional.

The moment theorem assumes a periodic spatial torus, C¹ density and velocity-independent acceleration, uniform decay exponent N>6 on compact time slabs, and a source Q with vanishing number, momentum and squared-speed moments. It does not require Q to be the selected homogeneous gain.

load_bearing.statement: For f,g∈X, the gain is representative-independent and bilinear, with ‖G(f,g)‖₁,w₀≤2‖f‖₁,w₀‖g‖₁,w₀. For nonnegative f of mass M, its gain has mass M², momentum M∫vf dv and squared-speed moment M∫|v|²f dv. For M=1 and the four stated absolute-integrability conditions, ∫φ(G(f,f)−f)dv=¼∫(B−A)Δφ dμ. The reflection preserves pair momentum, pair squared speed and measure; μ has full support, and every elastic pair is attained by one reflection.

For fixed u and 0<a<b, every element of the X-closed convex Gaussian-mixture class has a smooth representative with the stated uniform positive Gaussian lower bound, Gaussian upper bound and polynomial-Gaussian derivative bounds. Every sequence has a subsequence converging locally uniformly with all velocity derivatives. G(f,g) belongs to the same class whenever f and g do.

Under Countable Choice, for λ>0 and nonnegative normalized f₀∈X, there is a unique global X-continuous mild solution taking values in K, preserving mass, first moment and second moment. If f₀ belongs to the specified Gaussian-mixture class, its positive smooth representatives retain the Gaussian bounds, depend continuously on time locally uniformly in velocity, are C¹ in time and satisfy the collision equation pointwise.

For the specified equal mixture of isotropic Gaussians with distinct variances 0<a<b, H(t)=∫f_t log(v₀³f_t)dv is finite and continuously differentiable, with H′(t)=−λ/4∫(B−A)log(B/A)dμ≤0. Equality holds exactly when f_t is a normalized isotropic Gaussian; every such Gaussian is stationary, and H′(0)<0 for the specified mixture.
For a nonnegative phase-space density with positive finite number density and finite third velocity moment, define ρ=mn, u=n⁻¹∫vF dv, Π=m∫(v−u)⊗(v−u)F dv, e=½trΠ and q=m/2∫|v−u|²(v−u)F dv.

Under the stated periodicity, C¹ regularity, N>6 velocity decay, velocity-independent acceleration and vanishing source moments, the kinetic equation yields the displayed exact mass, momentum, total-energy and internal-energy balances. These identities supply no constitutive relation for Π or q, closure, or hydrodynamic limit.
